criteria_results.evidence: Created tests/integration/test_memory_episode_live.py with 4 integration tests. All tests are marked with pytestmark = [pytest.mark.integration, pytest.mark.asyncio(loop_scope='module')] at module level, ensuring every test in the file is properly marked for integration testing.

criteria_results.criterion_text: The test publishes via a connected `NATSClient.publish_episode()` and self-subscribes
criteria_results.evidence: All tests create a NATSClient instance, reuse the nats_client fixture connection, and call client.publish_episode(episode). Each test also subscribes to the resolved memory.episode.{project_id}.{episode_type} subject using nats_client.subscribe(subject, cb=on_message) before publishing, creating a self-contained publish-subscribe round-trip within the same test.

criteria_results.criterion_text: The subscriber decodes the raw body with `MemoryEpisodeV1.model_validate_json` and asserts
criteria_results.evidence: All subscriber callbacks use MemoryEpisodeV1.model_validate_json(msg.data) to decode the raw message body. The tests then assert that the decoded episode fields match the original published episode, verifying episode_id, project_id, episode_type, content_format, body, and all optional fields as appropriate for each test case.

criteria_results.criterion_text: The test does **not** assert JetStream server-side dedupe and does **not** point at the
criteria_results.evidence: The tests use direct NATS pub-sub without JetStream stream setup. They do not verify Nats-Msg-Id deduplication behavior and do not create or reference any JetStream streams. The tests simply publish episodes and subscribe to the core NATS subjects, demonstrating the basic message contract without JetStream-specific features.
